 Detailed Forecast
 Synopsis
 A high pressure system northeast of the Hawaiian Islands will continue to weaken and drift eastward. A low level trough passing through the islands will continue to produce periods of showers across the state with light to moderate rainfall amounts favoring windward and mountain areas of all islands. Two passing upper level disturbances will keep wet trade wind weather in the forecast through the end of this week. The subtropical ridge will settle in over the island chain by next week Monday with drying trends forecast for the first half of next week.
 Discussion
 A long band of unsettled clouds associated with a low level trough continues to produce widespread shower activity across the Hawaiian Islands this morning. Expect these periods of showers to continue through tonight as these clouds are lifted up over island mountains. Light to moderate rainfall amounts will favor windward mountain areas of each island, some of the stronger showers with this cloud band will produce rainfall over typically drier leeward areas along western island slopes.
Two upper level troughs will dig into the Hawaii region on Wednesday and Friday, keeping wet trade winds in the forecast into the weekend. Two surface high pressure centers will pass from west to east far north of the state during this time period. The latest global weather model solutions show these passing systems will produce moderate to breezy trade winds each day. Trade wind speeds will strengthen on Thursday and then peak just below advisory thresholds on Friday. Easterly trade winds trend lower for the first half of next week as the subtropical ridge settles in over the island chain, lowering subsidence temperature inversion heights to around 4,000 to 5,000 feet, and decreasing shower trends.
 Aviation
 Moderate to locally breezy trades will persist today as an old frontal boundary continues to move through the state. Expect pockets of low clouds clouds and showers to affect mainly windward and mountain areas, though some activity could spill over the terrain and onto leeward locations. MVFR ceilings and visibilities will accompany some of the more robust shower activity. Weather conditions should generally improve during the day with low clouds and numerous windward showers filling in again tonight.
AIRMET Sierra remains in effect above 2000 feet for north through east sections of all islands due to low clouds and showers.
AIRMET Tango remains in effect below 7000 feet for low level moderate turbulence over and downwind of island mountains.
 Marine
 Fresh to locally strong trade winds will continue to gradually ease today as robust high pressure far northeast of Hawaii slowly weakens and begins to consolidate with another high approaching from the northwest. The Small Craft Advisory (SCA) that had been in effect for all waters has been scaled back to the typically windy waters around Big Island and Maui along with windward waters near Oahu and Maui County where combined seas remain elevated due to a declining north swell. Moderate to locally strong trade winds will prevail tonight through Thursday, when the SCA will be limited to Big Island and Maui waters. Trades will briefly strengthen again late Thursday and Friday as a stronger high passes north of the state, then drop a notch during the weekend.
A moderate, medium period north (360 to 010 degrees) swell will gradually decline over the next couple of days. The bulk of the energy has been focused over the eastern end of the state, but the PacIOOS Hilo buoy indicates that the swell is down to 6 feet at 13 seconds, which is low enough to cancel the High Surf Advisory that was in place for Big Island and Maui. Expect north shore surf on all islands to slowly decline today and fade late Wednesday. A Marine Weather Statement continues to highlight declining moderate surges at Kahului and Hilo harbors today. A small north- northwest swell will be possible during the weekend, with a larger swell possible next Tuesday.
Rough surf along east-facing shores will remain above seasonal average today due to elevated trade wind swell and some wrapping north swell. East shore surf is expected to be around seasonal average Wednesday and Thursday, followed by a brief and slight increase Friday and Saturday. Mainly small background level surf will persist along south-facing shores during the next several days, with a small long-period swell possible on Friday.
 Fire weather
 A wet trade wind weather pattern lasting into the weekend will keep humidity levels below critical fire thresholds for most of the windier areas for the foreseeable future. Temperature inversion heights near Maui and the Big Island today will range from 8,000 to 9,000 feet elevation.
 HFO Watches/Warnings/Advisories
 Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM HST this evening for Oahu Windward Waters, Kaiwi Channel, Maui County Windward Waters, Big Island Windward Waters.
Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM HST Thursday for Maalaea Bay, Pailolo Channel, Alenuihaha Channel, Big Island Leeward Waters, Big Island Southeast Waters.
